meta.title: Three Ways In
meta.subtitle: The same runtime, reached in-process, as a child process, or over a socket.

views.label: 1 · In the same process
views.note: Import run() and await it. Lowest latency, real Python objects, simplest debugging. Everything else is built on this.

views.label: 2 · As a child process
views.note: JSON-RPC over pipes, the shape MCP and ACP use. Choose it when your product is not Python.

views.label: 3 · Over a socket
views.note: JSON-RPC over HTTP with events on SSE. Loopback-only by default until the per-run token is built.

views.label: 4 · The ports invert
views.note: Out of process, the host drives and the runtime calls back: judge, complete, invoke and propose are answered by you.

views.label: 5 · What it drives
views.note: Your components, and other agents made governable — either driven over ACP, or given your registry as an MCP server.

cards.title: 1 — Embedded, in your process
items: You write: ports = Ports(model=…, components=(…), governance=…, sink=…, clock=…) then async for event in run(plan, ports, options=…)
You get: the lowest latency, real Python objects, and the simplest debugging
Choose it when your product is Python and lives in the same process. Every other way is built on this one
run() is a plain async function, so a larger orchestration you already own can await it as one governed sub-part

cards.title: 2 — A child process over stdio
items: You get: JSON-RPC 2.0 on stdin and stdout — the same shape MCP and ACP use
Choose it when your product is not Python, or you want the runtime behind its own crash boundary
The direction inverts: you send run and resume; the runtime calls back for judge, complete, invoke and propose

cards.title: 3 — A server you connect to
items: You get: JSON-RPC over HTTP, with the run's events and the runtime's callbacks arriving on SSE
Two directions, two paths, because an HTTP server cannot call its client. Each connection gets its own session
Choose it when the client is on another machine
Stated honestly: loopback-only by default, refusing another bind without a token, because the per-run token is designed but not built

cards.title: What stays the same in all three
items: The same package, the same seven-move step, the same eleven event kinds
Every port argument and return already round-trips through JSON, which is why the wire was a composition root and not a rewrite
The wire passes the in-process test suite through a loopback transport, or it is not considered done

cards.title: And two ways to make other agents governable
items: Drive one: the ACP adapter runs Codex or Claude Code as an ordinary governed component
Serve one: the recording adapter offers your live registry to a child agent as an MCP server, so what it does is routed and therefore on your record
The difference is posture — what routes through you is controlled; what an agent does natively and reports is only observed
